nodes.name: Chemical Precipitation
nodes.procedure: Desulfurization wastewater samples are collected and analyzed to determine pollutant composition. The pH is adjusted using neutralizing agents such as Ca(OH)2. Precipitants including Ca(OH)2, NaOH, FeCl3, and AlCl3 are added to react with sulfides and suspended matter to form insoluble precipitates. Precipitates are formed and dispersed by stirring/mixing, then separated by filtration from the treatment tank.

unit_operations.name: pH Adjustment
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the pH of the wastewater is adjusted, usually by adding a neutralizing agent Ca(OH)2

unit_operations.name: Precipitation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: These chemicals react with sulfides, suspended matter, etc. in the wastewater to form insoluble precipitates

unit_operations.name: Solid-Liquid Separation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the precipitate is separated from the treatment tank by filtration

nodes.source_text: The chemical precipitation method mainly removes pollutants such as heavy metals and suspended solids from desulfurization wastewater through neutralization, precipitation... the precipitate is separated from the treatment tank by filtration.

nodes.name: Hybrid Zero-Valent Iron Treatment
nodes.procedure: Hybrid zero-valent iron (HZVI) technology is used to treat Se, Hg, nitrate, and other substances that are difficult to remove completely from desulfurization wastewater. The technology produces a self-sustaining, highly reactive mixture that can be used in near-neutral pH environments.
nodes.source_text: Huang et al. proposed the use of hybrid zero-valent iron (HZVI) technology to treat Se, Hg, nitrate... The technology is capable of rapid reduction, transformation, immobilization, and mineralization of each heavy metal...

nodes.name: Two-Stage Desalination Precipitation
nodes.procedure: First stage: CaO is added to desulfurization wastewater to remove Mg2+ and part of SO42−. Second stage: remaining SO42− and 48.1% Cl− are precipitated as calomel and Friedel's salt.

unit_operations.name: Stage 1 Precipitation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: In the first stage, the addition of CaO effectively removed Mg2+ and part of SO42−

unit_operations.name: Stage 2 Precipitation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: in the second stage, the remaining SO42− and 48.1% Cl− were precipitated as calomel and Friedel's salt

nodes.name: Evaporation Crystallization with Pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Sodium sulfate is added to desulfurization wastewater during pretreatment stage. The effluent is then pumped into evaporation crystallization device where gypsum crystallization occurs to produce high-purity sodium chloride crystals.

unit_operations.name: Pretreatment
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: In the pretreatment stage, sodium sulfate was added to the water

unit_operations.name: Evaporation Crystallization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the effluent was pumped into the evaporation crystallization device to prepare high-purity sodium chloride based on the method of gypsum crystallization

nodes.source_text: Li et al... In the pretreatment stage, sodium sulfate was added to the water, and then the effluent was pumped into the evaporation crystallization device to prepare high-purity sodium chloride based on the method of gypsum crystallization.
